useCase.name: Turn marks into grades automatically, and control when the result becomes visible to families

intent.name: grade.bands.define
intent.summary: Define the grade bands applied to one subject in this exam. One step, and the bands must cover nought to a hundred without overlapping.
routesHere: set the grade bands for maths — A is 80 to 100, B is 70 to 79

routesHere.text: maths ke grade bands set kar do
routesHere.gloss: set the grade bands for maths

routesHere.text: A grade 80 se 100, B 70 se 79 rakh do
routesHere.gloss: make A 80 to 100 and B 70 to 79

routesHere.text: pichle imtihan wale bands isi par laga do
routesHere.gloss: apply the same bands as the last exam

routesHere: define the bands for my subject in the first term exam

routesElsewhere.note: A grade is never adjusted by hand. It follows from the mark by the bands, so the same marks always produce the same grade (BR-3, BR-10).
Bands turn marks into grades. Whether a family sees the result is the Coordinator's separate decision (BR-6).
The passing marks are fixed when the exam is created (UC-06-01 BR-3). Bands are about grades, not about passing.

steps.note: One step. The teacher defines the bands applied to their own subject in this exam (BR-1) — bands set centrally and applied to a practical paper and a theory paper alike measure neither well.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Overlaps and gaps are enforced by the API and each error names the percentages at fault.
plan.atomicity: One write: the bands and the audit entry together or not at all. The bands used are recorded with the result (BR-11), so a grade awarded this term stays explainable after the bands have changed.

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. That subject is not in this exam, or is not assigned to the actor.

parameters.notes: The subject, which the acting teacher teaches (BR-1).

parameters.name: bands
parameters.notes: Each band: its grade, its lower percentage, its upper percentage and what it means. Together they must cover nought to a hundred with no overlap and no gap (BR-2). Every boundary is the teacher's — a planner that filled in a customary scale has set what an A means at this school.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: bands
fields.description: Each grade with its range and description, as recorded.

fields.name: students_regraded
fields.description: Students whose grade changed because the bands changed. Grades are recalculated by the same bands, never adjusted by hand (BR-10).

errors.note: The message names the overlapping ranges. A percentage that falls in two bands has no grade (BR-2).

errors.meaning: The bands leave a gap between nought and a hundred.
errors.note: The message names the uncovered range. A percentage that falls in none has no grade (BR-2).

planningRules.rule: Never invent a band or a boundary. What an A means at this school is the teacher's decision for their own subject (BR-1), and a customary 80-to-100 supplied by a planner grades every child in the class.
Never close a gap or trim an overlap on the actor's behalf. E1 and E2 are BR-2 working — report the exact percentages at fault and let the teacher say what they meant.
Never plan a grade change by hand. There is no such control (E8): a grade always follows from a mark through the bands (BR-3, BR-10).
Copy bands only where the actor named the exam to copy from. "The same as last time" is a lookup somebody has to confirm, not an assumption (A5).

Report how many students' grades changed where bands are redefined after marks exist. The recalculation is automatic (BR-10), and a teacher adjusting a boundary by a point should see how many children it moved.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Bands are redefined rather than withdrawn, and the recalculation follows. The bands used stay recorded with each result so an earlier grade remains explainable (BR-11).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The bands are recorded against this exam's maths results. They are kept with each result, so a grade awarded now stays explainable after the bands change (BR-11).

inputs.bands: as stated, with 80 in both A and B

steps.note: Emitted as stated. The API returns BANDS_OVERLAP (E1) — the overlap is not trimmed on the teacher's behalf (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is saved. Report that 80 falls in both bands and ask which it belongs to — a percentage in two bands has no grade.

resolvedPlans.outcome: The bands are copied and recorded against this exam's results in their own right (A5). Report them back in full — they are being applied to a different paper, and a boundary that suited last term's may not suit this one.

intent.name: exam.results.approve
intent.summary: Approve the results and release them, which is the moment families see a grade. Coordinator only, one step.
routesHere: approve and release the class 8 results

routesHere.text: natija manzoor kar ke shaya kar do
routesHere.gloss: approve the result and release it

request.gloss: the results are not accepted, send them back

routesElsewhere.note: Releasing makes the result visible; locking freezes it after the correction period (BR-9).
The total, the percentage and the grade are calculated on upload (BR-3). There is nothing to ask for.

request.text: kisi ek bache ka natija jari karo

routesElsewhere.note: A release covers the class. Each student and guardian then sees their own grade alone (BR-7).

steps.note: One step, and it reaches every family in the class. Nothing is visible to students or guardians before this, and a grade seen before the school agreed it cannot be unseen (BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An unclassified absence blocks that student's calculation and arrives as an error naming them; a Teacher attempting the release is refused.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the approval and the release together or not at all. Each student and guardian then sees their own grade alone (BR-7). Students with incomplete results are released too — an incomplete result stays incomplete until a makeup is marked, and saying so is more honest than hiding it (BR-5, E9).

errors.note: No grade can be calculated for it (E3). The message names the subjects.

planningRules.rule: Never release before the Coordinator has said so. A grade seen before the school agreed it cannot be unseen (BR-6), and this single call puts a number in front of every family in the class.

Never classify an absence to clear the way. E4 names students whose absence has not been decided as excused or unexcused, and that decision changes their percentage (BR-4) — it belongs to whoever knows why the child was away.
Report the incomplete results plainly. An incomplete result stays incomplete until a makeup is marked, and a percentage over fewer subjects is not comparable with a full one (BR-5).
Never plan a grade calculation. The total, the percentage and the grade are calculated on upload, so the same marks always produce the same grade (BR-3).
Never release a single student's result. The release covers the class, and each family then sees their own child's grade alone (BR-7).

reversal.statement: A release is not withdrawn. A result corrected afterwards is recalculated by the same bands and republished with the change visible, rather than quietly replaced (BR-12). The controller must not attempt a compensating call — families have already seen it.

plan.atomicity: One write: the return, its reason and the audit entry together or not at all. It goes back to the teacher, who corrects and recalculates. No student or guardian is told anything, because nothing was ever visible to them (BR-6).

plan.atomicity: One write: the lock and the audit entry together or not at all. It freezes what was published (BR-8). Nothing changes for a family — they already see the result; this closes the window in which it could change.

intent.summary: Reopen a locked result so a wrong one can be put right. School Admin only, one step, and it carries a reason.

routesElsewhere.note: A grade is never adjusted by hand. Correcting the mark recalculates the grade by the same bands (BR-10).
The two locks are separate and so are the two reopenings (BR-8).

steps.note: One step, and only this step. The marks are reopened, the correction made and the result recalculated and republished before being locked again — each act on its own (A6).

plan.atomicity: One write: the reopening, its reason and the audit entry together or not at all. The result becomes changeable again. What families already saw stays visible; a correction is republished with the change shown rather than quietly replacing it (BR-12).

planningRules.rule: Never chain a reopening onto a refused correction. The lock exists so that changing a published result is deliberate (BR-9), and a plan that reopened, corrected and relocked in one breath would make it decorative.
Never compose the reason. It is the record of why a published result was unfrozen, and a family asking how their child's grade changed is answered from it.
Report how many families have already seen the result. A correction is republished with the change visible (BR-12), so they will see both — which is the point, and worth knowing before starting.
Never relock in the same plan. The marks reopening, the correction and the recalculation all happen in between (A6).
